identity.title: A Noncorotating Gas Component in an Extreme Starburst at z = 4.3

paper_type_evidence.quote: ALMA 0.17 and 0.09 arcsec resolution observations of \[C ii\] emission clearly demonstrate that the gas kinematics is characterized by an ordered rotation.

evidence.quote: a bright unlensed submillimeter galaxy at $z=4.3$, COSMOS-AzTEC-1, hosting a compact starburst

question.value: Does the z=4.3 compact starburst SMG COSMOS-AzTEC-1 contain off-center gas components, and are they corotating with the disk (in-situ clumps vs. ex-situ accretion)?

evidence.quote: we report the detection of a non-corotating subcomponent in a bright SMG at $z=4.3$, COSMOS-AzTEC-1
ALMA Band-7 observations of COSMOS-AzTEC-1 with a central frequency of 350 GHz (860 $\mu$m)
the other two detect \[C ii\] 158 $\mu$m and OH 163 $\mu$m emission lines

baselines.value: compact 15 m–2.5 km; extended 178 m–14.6 km

evidence.quote: The compact and extended configuration observations cover the baseline lengths of 15 m – 2.5 km and 178 m – 14.6 km, respectively.
resulting in a spatial resolution of 0.$''$$17\times$0.$''$16

sensitivity.value: 46 uJy/beam continuum; 0.40 and 0.45 mJy/beam per channel in low/high-res cubes

evidence.quote: The noise levels in the low- and high-resolution cubes are 0.40 mJy beam$^{-1}$ per channel and 0.45 mJy beam$^{-1}$ per channel, respectively.
The integration time is $\sim$30 minutes in both configurations.

what.value: Previous 0.3'' [C II] cube kinematic fit and CO(4-3) size, 1.1 mm source search

evidence.quote: The kinematic parameters agree well with those derived from the previous fitting of a 0.3$''$-resolution \[C ii\] cube with a channel width of 50 km s$^{-1}$

what.value: [C I]-based gas mass of 7.2e10 Msun within 2.5 kpc

evidence.quote: the \[C i\]-based gas mass of $7.2\times10^{10}~M_\odot$ is mostly enclosed inside a radius of 2.5 kpc
We calibrate the data in the standard manner using `CASA`
using the `CASA/tclean` task
We also adopt `Multi-Scale Clean` algorithm

weighting_robust.value: robust=+2.0 with uvtaper 0.05'' (continuum); robust=+2.0, uvtaper 0.1'' (low-res cube)

evidence.quote: Cleaning with weighting of `robust`=+2.0 and `uvtaper`=0.$''$05 results in a spatial resolution of 0.$''$09$\times$0.$''$09

masking.value: circular mask 1'' diameter, cleaned to 1 sigma

evidence.quote: We clean the map down to the 1$\sigma$ level in a circular mask with a diameter of 1$''$

array_combination.value: concat in uv plane; compact weights scaled by 0.2 for continuum, unscaled for cubes

evidence.quote: We decrease the absolute visibility weights of the compact data by 0.2

unstated_but_needed: line-free channels / continuum subtraction for cubes

method.value: Combine compact and extended data; tclean with robust=+2 and taper; 30 km/s channels

evidence.quote: we make low- and high-resolution clean cubes with a channel width of 30 km s$^{-1}$

validation.value: Visibility amplitude comparison between configs (Appendix A)

evidence.quote: There is no systematic offset in the amplitude of the vector-averaged visibilities between the compact and extended configuration data

analysis_steps.goal: Fit dust continuum disk and clumps

method.value: Sersic (plus point source or Gaussian) fits with 7 free parameters; residual search

evidence.quote: while the sky value is fixed to be zero
Six of 300 simulated residual maps show positive or negative 5$\sigma$ emission

analysis_steps.goal: Fit [CII] disk kinematics and find residuals

method.value: 3D thick disk with arctan rotation curve fit to low-res cube, subtract, search residual channel maps

evidence.quote: We assume a thick disk and an arctan rotation curve in the models.
are fitted to the data cube using a Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) algorithm

method.value: Velocity-integrated maps over >2 sigma range; elliptical Gaussian fit

We derive 0.17$\pm$0.04 Jy km s$^{-1}$ for \[C ii\]-1 and 0.62$\pm$0.10 Jy km s$^{-1}$ for \[C ii\]-2 by using CASA/`imfit`, which fits an elliptical gaussian component on the image.

findings_qualitative.value: [CII]-2 is offset by ~200 km/s, lies along the kinematic minor axis, 2 kpc from the disk; interpreted as infalling gas

evidence.quote: The spatial and velocity offset suggest that \[C ii\]-2 is falling into COSMOS-AzTEC-1 from a direction perpendicular to the disk rotation.

claims.hypothesis: Are there non-corotating gas components in the starburst disk?
claims.experiment: Galpak3D disk fit to [CII] cube and residual channel maps, with simulations and dirty-cube checks
claims.result: Two residual components above 5 sigma in two adjacent channels; [CII]-2 offset by ~200 km/s along minor axis

evidence.quote: \[C ii\]-2 has a velocity offset of $\sim200$ km s$^{-1}$ from the coherent velocity of the disk

claims.hypothesis: Are low S/N dust clumps from earlier work real?
claims.result: Only two bright clumps recovered; other 8 not detected
claims.finding: Low S/N clumps may be noise artifacts

evidence.quote: other 8 low S/N (4–5$\sigma$) clumps were not detected in the residual map

limitations_admitted.value: [CII]-1 could be an artifact of disk asymmetry; deeper observations needed

evidence.quote: It requires deeper observations to distinguish whether or not \[C ii\] -1 truly represents a separate component from the overall disk rotation.

referee_caveats_inferred: Single-pointing short integration; residual significance depends on idealized disk model
Mass ratio inferred from [CII] flux ratio only

reproducibility.score_reason: Public data and named tools, but several imaging and fitting settings are missing.
reproducibility.rediscovery_reason: Key fitting details are not given and the main result is a qualitative residual detection.

companion_papers.why: Earlier ALMA data and clump identification
